rec.subject: Physics
rec.question: An electron and a proton are moving under the influence of mutual forces. In calculating the change in the kinetic energy of the system during motion, one ignores the magnetic force of one on another. This is because
rec.option1: the two magnetic forces are equal and opposite, so they produce no net effect.
rec.option2: the magnetic forces do no work on each particle.
rec.option3: the magnetic forces do equal and opposite (but non-zero) work on each particle.
rec.option4: the magnetic forces are necessarily negligible.
rec.correct_option: the magnetic forces do no work on each particle.

rec.question: A proton is kept at rest. A positively charged particle is released from rest at a distance $d$ in its field. Consider two experiments; one in which the charged particle is also a proton and in another, a positron. In the same time $t$, the work done on the two moving charged particles is
rec.option1: same as the same force law is involved in the two experiments.
rec.option2: less for the case of a positron, as the positron moves away more rapidly and the force on it weakens.
rec.option3: more for the case of a positron, as the positron moves away a larger distance.
rec.option4: same as the work done by charged particle on the stationary proton.
rec.correct_option: more for the case of a positron, as the positron moves away a larger distance.

Initially M$_2$ is at rest and M$_1$ is moving toward M$_2$ with speed $v$ and collides head-on with M$_2$ (through the spring). Which statement is correct?
rec.option1: While the spring is fully compressed, all the KE of M$_1$ is stored as PE of the spring.
rec.option2: While the spring is fully compressed, the system momentum is not conserved, though final momentum is equal to initial momentum.
rec.option3: If the spring is massless, the final state of M$_1$ is a state of rest.
rec.option4: If the surface on which the blocks are moving has friction, then the collision cannot be elastic.
rec.correct_option: If the spring is massless, the final state of M$_1$ is a state of rest.
